Timeline

Changes

What changed, newest first. Each entry is drawn from the project's changelog.

  1. 14 Oct 2026

    The ArduPilot rail and the city demonstration recorded on video, the detector found off the car, and figures of the whole system

    • The usual red-car demonstration with the no-fly zone and the policy indicator was re-flown on the current code and recorded, 260 s: P0 escape rate 0.0, 0.0 s inside the zone, the car within 30 m for 0.991 of the time (0.977 and 0.985 on the 3 Oct flights with the zone) and a minimum separation of 12.0 m. The follow controller never commanded a P0 violation on this flight, so the zero escape rate does not show the Shield at work. As on 3 Oct, a hand-written follow controller is the pilot and Project AirSim's own flight controller flies the drone.
    • The ArduPilot rail was recorded for the first time, flying the close approach to the red car with the Shield on and off (Project AirSim + ArduPilot SITL commanded over pymavlink, none of the grant's topologies). Shield on: 0 P0 escape ticks in the 388 ticks the Shield flew; the escalation braked, then sent the aircraft home, and ArduPilot's return to launch flew the rest of the 517 ticks. Shield off, the same pilot: 736 P0 escape ticks of 1099 (rate 0.6697), its command flown into the building-clearance margin. The escape count judges each command the Shield sent, not where the aircraft was: with the Shield on, the aircraft still stood inside a P0 margin on 71 of the 517 ticks (20 while the Shield flew, up to 1.0 m deep, and 51 under ArduPilot's return to launch), against 739 with the Shield off; a forecast that starts from the aircraft's own velocity is next.
    • On 13 Oct the simulator's pose of the car and the detector's estimates lay far apart, and it was open which one was wrong. On 14 Oct it was settled: the pose was right, and the detector was not on the car. The recorded video shows its box on a red traffic signal; across the close flights, 0 estimates came within 6 m of the car, and on the 13 Oct Shield-on flight the car was in the camera's view on 10 of the 149 estimate ticks. So these flights test the Shield, not tracking.
    • The perception node now records the drone's camera with the policy indicator and a chase camera, outside the control loop: with a CPU-bound stand-in for the detector the loop ran at 9.12 Hz while recording and 9.15 Hz without.
    • Figures of the whole system, drawn from code: the end-to-end flow, the components, the topologies and one Shield tick, now on the How it works and work-package pages.

  2. 13 Oct 2026

    Gate G1 passes again after the fence change, and a close approach flown with the Shield on and off

    • Gate G1 passed again after ArduPilot's fence settings changed: 3/3 runs met every condition, ArduPilot's position estimate stayed within 0.82-0.83 m (p95) of the simulator's true position against the 1.0 m limit and 18.96-18.98 m for a position frozen at the start, with 0 fence breaches and 0 airborne collisions.
    • A 120 s close approach to the red car with an aggressive test pilot, on Project AirSim + ArduPilot SITL over pymavlink (none of the grant's topologies), flying a signed policy bundle for the first time on this rail. Shield on: 0 P0 escape ticks over a 532-tick flight, part of it flown by ArduPilot's BRAKE hold and return to launch; the escalation held the aircraft in ArduCopter's BRAKE mode at 7.99-8.01 m, the first flight evidence for that hold, but in the second hold the depth of the violation kept growing (2.95 m in 2.07 s), so the escalation sent it home. The aircraft stood inside a P0 margin only while ArduPilot flew the hold and the return, never while the Shield flew. Shield off, the same pilot and route: P0 escape rate 0.661, the rail's first Shield-off control.
    • The detector was not on the car in these flights (found on 14 Oct), so they test the Shield, not tracking.

  3. 13 Oct 2026

    The grant's forecast in the stress harness, rule clocks and rule changes on the flying rails, and the WP4 outputs

    • The stress harness now checks every command against the grant's 5 s forecast at 0.1 s steps (50 future poses), and flies velocity commands through a model of ArduPilot's position controller.
    • The ArduPilot SITL rails and the perception node give the Shield a rule clock, so time windows and switches take effect in flight, and the SITL rails serve the REST endpoint for rule changes during a flight.
    • The flight rails fly a signed policy bundle by default, and the perception node uploads the policy's zones to ArduPilot's GeoFence before arming.
    • The Shield builds a moving no-fly zone only where the forecast can meet it: in 200 checks it builds 199 moving zones instead of 9600, with the same decisions.
    • The stress harness's control plane offers the grant's 10 gRPC calls, and episodes export to step and episode records with the grant's field names.
    • Headless and desktop measurements only when this entry was written; of these, the signed policy bundle has since flown (the later 13 Oct entry above).

  4. 9 Oct 2026 – 12 Oct 2026

    Rule-change templates, a cost map, both hashes, a harness control plane and the Orin defined for JetPack 6.2

    • The moving no-fly zone, the time-window switch, the corridor swap and the circle fence compile into the rule summary, and a policy file with a switch or a swap loads for flight.
    • A cost-map adapter draws a policy in the grant's conventions; on 24 project policies, 0 points that the Shield forbids were priced cheaper than the grant's conventions allow.
    • Every bundle carries both the project's hash and the reference implementation's hash, and a forged reference entry is refused 29/29.
    • The escalation's hold step is now flown as ArduCopter's BRAKE mode, which held 14.97-15.01 m in ArduPilot SITL with no pilot input.
    • The stress harness takes its episode calls over gRPC with mutual TLS (headless harness, no simulator).
    • The Jetson Orin deployment is defined for JetPack 6.2: ROS 2 Jazzy in an Ubuntu 24.04 container, with rclpy on Python 3.12.

  5. 8 Oct 2026

    Gate G1 passed: ArduPilot flies Project AirSim, and Mission Planner's port carries the flight

    • ArduPilot SITL now flies the Project AirSim drone through the simulator's own ArduPilot controller, and mavlink-router passes its MAVLink stream to Mission Planner's UDP port 14550 and to the perception node.
    • Gate G1 passed on 3 runs of the same square mission: ArduPilot's position estimate stayed within 0.81-0.82 m (p95) of the simulator's true position, against a 1.0 m limit and 18.9-19.0 m for a position frozen at the start, and its motor commands lifted the vehicle 14.5 m from rest.
    • Each AUTO square mission (10 m sides, 15 m up) reached all 5 mission items with no airborne collision and landed within 0.2 m of take-off; ArduPilot ran at 0.958-0.967 of real time.
    • A 120 s red-car follow flew with the camera, the detector, the Shield and the escalation state machine commanding ArduPilot over MAVLink directly (not yet through MAVROS 2). Mission Planner's UDP port received position and attitude at 19.0 Hz for the whole mission, with no gap longer than 0.1 s.
    • All on one desktop: development runs, not KPI figures. The grant measures its KPIs on the hil topology (Jetson Orin).

  6. 7 Oct 2026

    The grant's policy form, a Shield that escalates, rule changes during a flight and the ROS 2 interface

    • Policies written in the grant's own form load as written; every rule type the grant lists can be declared, and circle no-fly zones are enforced.
    • Regulation, site and mission layers merge into one policy, and an override that would loosen a lower layer's hard rule is refused.
    • Validation is strict: 35/35 malformed policies in the negative test set are refused; the loader of 5 Oct 2026 refused 20/35 (14/25 of the 25 earlier cases).
    • The escalation state machine (Brake, Loiter, RTL, Land) runs inside the Shield on every tick, and each repair reports its size so that the grant's θ applies.
    • Rule changes during a flight: a moving no-fly zone, a time-window switch and a corridor swap, each starting a new policy generation, also through a REST endpoint.
    • The grant's ROS 2 interface: body-frame actions end to end, a MAVLink adapter node that publishes PositionTarget to MAVROS 2, launch files, a router configuration for Mission Planner beside MAVROS 2, and ArduPilot's GeoFence as the backstop.
    • The Shield looks 5 s ahead at 0.1 s steps, as the grant specifies; at the grant's load (50 rules, 50 poses) a check near a fence takes 0.39 ms and a full Shield step 2.5 ms on the development desktop.
    • The stress harness runs every event type the grant names in the middle of a headless episode (no simulator), with RTL and Land outcomes, from 16 scenario templates, one file each.

  7. 6 Oct 2026

    Shield speed, a typed rule summary, a paraphraser, an escalation state machine and signed bundles

    • A compiled fence index: with 50 rules and a 3 s forecast at 0.5 s steps, one check near a fence takes 0.13-0.26 ms (median; was 14-33 ms).
    • The Constraint Summary Pack is typed, with the 14 locked fields, risk grading and a 256-token budget, and it can be placed before OpenVLA's instruction (54-106 tokens).
    • A paraphraser with 112 stored free-form paraphrases and a slot validator.
    • An escalation state machine, Normal → Brake → Loiter → RTL → Land, with the grant's defaults.
    • Ed25519-signed policy bundles, a full-length policy hash and a lock file of policy versions.
    • Stress profiles (smoke 52 × 1, nightly 211 × 3) and a KPI report that prints every score beside its baseline.

  8. 3 Oct 2026

    The policy on screen, and a no-fly zone in the city

    • An on-screen policy indicator: one row per rule with its limit, live value and status, an event banner and a north-up map.
    • A no-fly zone on the red car's route: on a 240 s flight the drone stayed out of it and kept the car within 30 m for 98.5 % of the mission (98.7 % on a flight without the zone; 8.8-43.6 % on 7 earlier flights with the old target selection).
    • A flowchart of the tracking pipeline.

  9. 30 Sep 2026

    Target identity and re-acquisition for the red-car follow

    • On 4 flights with the identity layer, the drone's estimate stayed on the red car on 99.6-100 % of served ticks; on 7 earlier flights, the old estimator replayed on the same detections managed 1.3-69.7 %.
    • A car seen beyond the re-acquisition range becomes a far lead that the search flies toward, until the normal gate can judge it.
    • The city's pedestrians stay on their routes over a 30-minute run.

  10. 29 Sep 2026

    Traffic signals that change, and pedestrians who wait

    • 258 of the city's 292 signal heads switch on a fixed-time plan, and the cars obey it.
    • 40 pedestrians walk routes, wait at the kerb for the walk phase and cross on the zebras.
    • After losing the car, the search flies the car's street to the next junction and watches each exit.
    • Landing sites are chosen from pavement cells checked as landable.

  11. 29 Sep 2026

    A map of the city, a trail to follow, and a steady 10 Hz

    • An obstacle map of the CityLife city (180 × 100 cells) for the Shield's clearance rule.
    • The follow controller flies the car's trail, so it turns where the car turned.
    • The control loop runs at 9.99-10.0 Hz on every flight (was 9.31-9.37 Hz on the red-car flights).

  12. 23 Sep 2026

    One red car to follow, and cars that keep left and give way

    • Exactly one red car drives a loop of the city, and the flight starts when the drone sees it.
    • Cars keep left and give way at junctions.
    • A ground-contact check was added for detection boxes that cannot be standing on the road (a red traffic signal had passed every other check as a car).

  13. 22 Sep 2026

    A city instead of a street

    • Follow missions fly in the CityLife city, with its own crowd and traffic.
    • Ground truth for the city's own people and cars is read back from the simulator, so a city flight logs it and can be scored.

  14. 10 Sep 2026 0.5.0

    A higher-resolution front camera

    • The front camera was raised from 400×225 to 768×432. Measured offline, the end-to-end detection step is faster than with the old setting (30.7 ms against 35.2 ms).

  15. 9 Sep 2026 0.4.0

    A steadier target estimate

    • The target estimator bounds a person's speed. On a replay of the pedestrian phase, the estimate was served on 257 of 331 ticks instead of 55.
    • Each stand-off ring is scored with true and false positives.

  16. 8 Sep 2026 0.3.0

    Replay bundles and a pinned action frame

    • Replay bundles that re-derive their own KPIs.
    • The boundary between the drone's body frame and the world frame is pinned by tests, with yaw rate in rad/s.
    • Obstacle maps are chosen by altitude band.

  17. 1 Sep 2026 – 7 Sep 2026 0.2.0

    A scenario sweep and policy bundles

    • A scenario sweep harness for the Shield.
    • Policy bundles, and policies anchored to WGS84 coordinates.
    • A start-up refusal for a rule that no target phrase can reach.

  18. 24 Aug 2026 – 31 Aug 2026 0.1.0

    The first Guardrail layer

    • The Policy DSL, the prefix compiler, the Safety Shield and stress-testing groundwork.
    • The Shield flown on ArduPilot SITL.
    • Obstacle maps built from the simulator, scripted city scenes with traffic and pedestrians, and a recorder that saves the drone's camera view beside a chase view.

As of 14 Oct 2026. Built from the project repository by tools/build_public_site.py.
